title: Why Philadelphia first: no job in New York yet
summary: After a back-and-forth, Waters confirms he went to Philadelphia only because the job offer came from there, having no New York work, and was tired of teaching, which was hurting his health.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: OK, not fully resolved but cleared up a little bit. Second: you made the statement that you left the Boston area to A, end your teaching career and B, take a crack at the big time which you defined as the Big Apple, New York City.
Yeah.
How come you didn't just go directly to New York, why did you go to Philadelphia first?
Well, I told you later on that I forgot about this big band. I said, I told you later on that I said that the first big band -
I understand, so let me say -
So that clears that -

So you're telling me that you, your general plan was to leave Boston, leave teaching, go to New York, but the first real opportunity to break it clean and leave Boston was a job that happened to be in Philadelphia so you said 'What the hell, I'll go to Philadelphia first'.
Benny Waters 50HP 4/6/82 65
Yeah.
That's the way it was, what I just said.

Well, I got a job in Philadelphia. I got this job in Philadelphia which I didn't, it came up from this guy, this guy which I don't remember the name, the violin player. That's who recommended me to Charlie -
But we're not talking about Charlie Johnson. You're in Boston -
You - well, what're you talking about then, you're talkin' Atlantic City, aren't you -
No, I'm not. I'm not talking about Atlantic City at all.
Oh, are you talkin' about the band in Philadelphia?
No, I'm not talking about any-
Well that's the only connection I have is Philadelphia and New York -
Slow down, let's go back to the beginnin'. You're in Boston. I asked you why did you leave Boston, and you said to get away from teaching -
Yeah -
and to take a crack at the big time, like New York City.
Yeah.
OK. So I said 'Well then why didn't you just go to New York, why did you go to Philadelphia?'
Well what, that's obviously, I didn't have no job in New York.
Right, so you got the job -
(laughs) That's obvious, I (laughs) -
I know it's obvious, that's what I'm tryin' to do, I'm trying to get you to say that that's the way it was, we can't have these things on the record from my authority -
Yeah -
I gotta have you to say it, I wasn't there -
I had no job -
Benny Waters JOHP 6/6/82

So you were in Boston and you got the offer from the job from Philadelphia. You would have preferred getting an offer from New York, but anything to get you away from Boston at the time would do and that's why you went to Philly.
Yeah. I got tired of teaching, that was the first thing I said, you remember.
Yeah, I know, I said it three times myself.
Yeah. So most likely I would have left anyway, regardless of, even if I didn't go to New York. I got tired of teachin', it was interferin' with my health also, I was nervous and everything -
Right -
